setup: Every number is measured here, on 2026-11-10, on one Apple M5 Mac (10 cores, 32 GB, macOS 27.0.1), with ouo and Sentry on the same app and journey per platform and a no-SDK baseline in every round. Web: headless Chromium 156 through Playwright 1.64.1, @ouo11y/browser 0.3.1 against @sentry/browser 11.11.0, 5 rounds (3 at 4x CPU throttling), host load about 2. iOS: Simulator (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.0), ouo11y-ios 0.3.0 against sentry-cocoa 9.33.0, 12 cold launches (about half at host load 10 to 139, while a discarded contended run's load was falling; the medians of the quiet launches match) and 3 journey rounds at host load about 2 to 3. Android: emulator (API 35, arm64), the Kotlin of sdk/android against sentry-android 8.63.0, 3 rounds, host load about 3 to 5. React Native: JS bundle size only. Simulator and emulator numbers are not device numbers. Medians; whiskers show the lowest and highest run.

charts.title: Web bundle
charts.intro: Each variant bundled the way an app bundler would (esbuild, minified, ESM, code splitting). "Initial" is what the page downloads at load; ouo loads rrweb lazily, so its replay cost is a second chunk fetched only when replay is sampled. Sentry was bundled with its replay in the main chunk, its default.

charts.title: With replay sampled: all JS downloaded, gzip
charts.note: ouo: the initial chunk plus the lazy rrweb chunk. A session without replay downloads only the initial chunk.

charts.title: React Native JS, gzip
charts.note: JS only, React Native and Expo packages external. Native code is extra (see the iOS and Android charts).

charts.title: Web runtime, 60 s journey, headless Chromium
charts.intro: Chromium 156.0.8078.4, no CPU throttling, 5 interleaved rounds per variant. Values are the SDK's added cost: the variant's median minus the no-SDK median. Whiskers are the lowest and highest run, also minus the no-SDK median.

charts.title: Init call on the main thread
charts.note: Synchronous time of the init call itself; work it schedules later is in the CPU charts.

charts.title: Renderer CPU added (main thread and workers)
Interaction task, p90, added
charts.note: The main-thread task that dispatched each click, key or wheel event: app handler plus SDK listeners and observers.

charts.title: Bytes sent, all ingest
charts.note: Request bodies as received by the fake collector (compressed where the SDK compresses), including the flush at page close.

charts.title: Web runtime with 4x CPU throttling
charts.intro: The same journey with Chrome's CPU throttled 4x, a rough stand-in for a mid-range phone; 3 rounds.

charts.title: Init call on the main thread (4x)
iOS Simulator
charts.intro: iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0: simulator numbers, not device numbers. One UIKit app built three ways (no SDK, ouo11y-ios 0.3.0, sentry-cocoa 9.33.0); replay is a runtime switch. Size is the arm64 device build. Init: 12 cold launches, about half of them at host load 10 to 139 (the medians of the quiet launches match). CPU, memory and bytes: 3 interleaved rounds of 20 s idle plus a 60 s timer-driven journey at host load about 2 to 3. Values are added over the no-SDK app; whiskers are the lowest and highest run, minus the no-SDK median. At n = 3, read only differences whose ranges do not overlap. Details: measure/ios/README.md.

charts.title: iOS: init on the main thread
Android emulator
charts.intro: Android emulator, API 35, arm64, 4 vCPU, software graphics. One native Kotlin app built per variant with R8. ouo here is the Kotlin code the React Native SDK vendors (signals and replay): it has no native exporter, so it sends replay only, while Sentry also sends errors, spans and sessions. CPU counts every thread but the render thread, because emulated graphics swamp total CPU. 3 interleaved rounds; whiskers are the lowest and highest run, minus the no-SDK median. Details: measure/android/README.md.

charts.title: Android: init on the main thread
Android: CPU added off the render thread, journey
charts.note: Every thread but RenderThread: the SDK threads plus the main, binder, JIT and GC work they cause.

charts.title: Android: steady memory added (PSS after settle)
charts.note: Peak PSS (five samples in the journey) moved by about 1 MiB between runs, more than the SDKs added, so the steady value is shown.

budgets.basis: Sentry: web 156; iOS 662 journey and 429 idle; Android 190. iOS journey: ouo's median is above Sentry's, but its lowest run is below, so at n = 3 ouo is possibly, not certainly, costlier. An idle screen should cost close to nothing
budgets.method: Paired deltas: each SDK run minus the no-SDK run of the same round. Web: run.mjs, 10 rounds, on PRs that touch sdk/browser and nightly on main; the web baseline alone spans 369 to 515 ms/min over 5 rounds, more than the 45 ms/min of headroom, so a single median is not a gate. Mobile: the B3 benchmark (docs/benchmarks.md), extended with native ouo11y-ios / sentry-cocoa and Android cells, N >= 10 with real taps, at release checkpoints. Fail only when the lower quartile of the paired deltas is above the budget. Regressions between releases use the B3 rule (docs/benchmarks.md section 5: worse by the threshold and outside the previous IQR)

not_measured.why: The harness ran Chromium only; the CDP metrics it reads do not exist elsewhere

Measuring it needs a release build of the Expo example app on a simulator and emulator, which did not fit this step. The JS bundle and the native pieces (iOS and Android harnesses) were measured separately
No phone was used. Simulator CPU and memory are the Mac's; the emulator renders in software

The SDK emits no browser.resource_timing events today; initial resources go out as resourceFetch child spans of documentLoad, always on, and are inside the measured telemetry bytes. Step 12 should price the event once it exists
3 journey rounds per variant (each round takes about 10 minutes on the simulator); medians with min and max over 3 runs

not_measured.what: App Store thinned / compressed download size
not_measured.why: no signing identity or App Store Connect; reported the unsigned device-arch (arm64) .app plus an IPA-shaped zip instead
simulator only by instruction: CPU and memory are the Mac's host process, network is loopback
the journey is timer-driven inside the app (no synthesised touches), so neither SDK's tap tracking ran

not_measured.what: Work done for the app by other processes (backboardd, render server, simulator networking)
not_measured.why: proc_pid_rusage counts the app process only

not_measured.what: ouo Android handled-error capture, HTTP spans, traces/logs/metrics export (OTLP) in the native host
not_measured.why: sdk/android has no native init, exporter or handled-error/HTTP API today; in the React Native SDK those live in JS (@ouo11y/react-native) and only replay + signals are native. The ouo variants therefore send replay chunks only; the handled error and the 3 HTTP calls per Fetch produce no ouo telemetry, while Sentry reports them (error event, OkHttp spans, transactions, sessions). Wire and CPU deltas are not like-for-like on that part.

not_measured.what: ouo signals' wire cost (crash / hang / termination reports)
not_measured.why: Signals writes crash.json/run.json and hands the previous run's report to the host at the next launch; the native host has no sender (the RN JS SDK sends it). No crash or hang was provoked in the journey.

not_measured.what: ouo full SDK as shipped (React Native app examples/ouo-mobile: JS SDK + native replay + signals)
not_measured.why: Not run: an RN app's own baseline (Hermes, RN runtime) would swamp a native comparison against sentry-android, and building the Expo example (prebuild + C++ build) was out of the time budget of this step. The native host measures exactly the Kotlin code the RN SDK vendors.

not_measured.what: Runtime cost of sentry-android with NDK (variant sentryfull)
not_measured.why: Measured for size only; the NDK handler adds a native crash handler, not per-minute work, and the runtime runs cover sentry-android-core (+replay).

not_measured.what: Device (real hardware) CPU, memory and energy
not_measured.why: Emulator only (no physical phone by rule). Guest GL is emulated (-gpu swiftshader_indirect), so the app's RenderThread burns ~13 s CPU per journey minute even in the baseline; PixelCopy and JPEG/MP4 encoding costs differ from a phone's GPU and hardware codecs (Sentry replay encodes MP4 through MediaCodec, here a software encoder). Battery/energy cannot be measured on an emulator.

not_measured.what: Frame timing (jank) impact via dumpsys gfxinfo, and simpleperf profiles
not_measured.why: Not collected: with emulated GL the frame times reflect the emulator, not the SDKs; per-thread /proc CPU attribution is used instead.
